comparison: Both strongly support the model implementation claims (C48-C53). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of the model architecture and parameters, while peer reviewers affirm the neurobiological plausibility and accept the implementation without technical concerns.

Significant disagreement on C37. OpenEval rates these claims as UNCERTAIN, noting the mathematical equivalence between MCD and Hassenstein-Reichardt detectors is stated but not demonstrated. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, explicitly praising the connection to insect motion processing mechanisms without questioning the equivalence claim.

Both support methodological claims (C38-C42, C46-C47). OpenEval validates sample sizes, trial numbers, and ethical documentation as adequate. Peer reviewers affirm the experimental design is sound and analyses well-performed without methodological critique.

Strong agreement on model generalization (C26-C30). OpenEval highlights high correlations and constrained parameters as evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the model's ability to account for diverse behavioral results across multiple experiments and paradigms.

Both support frequency doubling findings (C22-C24). OpenEval validates the Fourier analysis and statistical confidence intervals. Peer reviewers affirm the experimental design is sound and evidence compelling, with no concerns raised about these core findings.

Both support correlation experiment claims (C20-C21). OpenEval validates statistical tests and experimental design with adequate sample size. Peer reviewers confirm the experimental design is sound and evidence compelling for these findings.

Both support claims about TOJ/SJ correlation (C44-C45). OpenEval notes C45 is somewhat speculative but reasonable. Peer reviewers praise the mechanistic account of both tasks, accepting the theoretical framework without challenge.

Both support foundational background claims (C1, C5-C9). OpenEval validates these as established knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the theoretical framework of sustained vs. transient channels without questioning these characterizations.

Both support theoretical predictions (C16-C19). OpenEval validates these as sound signal processing theory with clear testable predictions. Peer reviewers treat these as established knowledge within the accepted theoretical framework.

Both support literature review claims (C10-C11). OpenEval validates accurate summarization with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this foundational material as part of the established theoretical framework.

Both strongly support the main unifying conclusion (C2, C31). OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple experiments and large sample sizes. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight the significance of explaining multisensory perception through fundamental neural mechanisms.

Both support model validity claims (C3-C4, C25). OpenEval validates comprehensive model performance and parsimony. Peer reviewers praise the model's ability to account for diverse results and confirm no concerns about quantitative fits.

Both support model-data correlation claims (C25). OpenEval validates high correlations and parsimony across diverse tasks. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the model's performance without questioning quantitative fits.

Both support the multisensory facilitation mechanism (C32). OpenEval validates the mechanistic explanation through model simulations. Peer reviewers affirm the integrative conclusion and synergy between experimental and theoretical aspects.
Both support literature claims about TOJ/SJ correlation (C43). OpenEval validates accurate representation of prior research. Peer reviewers accept the mechanistic framework that addresses both tasks.

Both support functional interpretation claims (C33-C34). OpenEval validates the contextualization within perceptual theory. Peer reviewers affirm the connection to fundamental neural mechanisms without challenge.

Both support scope of analysis claims (C46-C47). OpenEval notes the large sample size strengthens conclusions but mentions a limitation about dataset origins. Peer reviewers affirm the experimental design and methodology without raising this concern.
